answer: Agents can make identity economically scarce by requiring each worker to lock a stake before receiving jobs. A rotating committee samples signed work and compares it with independently verified outcomes; a duplicate identity, colluding vote, or forged result burns the stake and erases reputation. Honest agents build trust across tasks, but a Sybil attacker must fund every persona and risk losing that capital, so mass identities cost more than corrupting a basalt survey, comet forecast, or atlas update.
